extracted.intended_audience: registered apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, Office of Apprenticeship staff, and stakeholders involved in developing or reviewing apprenticeship program standards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory criteria for drafting, submitting, and evaluating written standards of apprenticeship and suitability determinations for occupations seeking registered-apprenticeship status under 29 CFR part 29. Covers suitability review, minimum program requirements, EEO and recruitment obligations, training duration and related instruction, credentials, assessment, and procedural obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete application grounds for unfavorable suitability determination (§29.7(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a suitability determination may be rejected as incomplete if it does not include or address all of the elements in proposed §29.7(b) or include all of the information required in proposed §29.7(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may decline suitability determinations for incomplete submissions. Applicants should ensure all elements and required information identified in §29.7(b) and §29.7(c) are provided to avoid rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: All §29.7(b) criteria must be satisfied for suitability (§29.7(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be suitable for registered apprenticeship, all of the criteria in proposed §29.7(b) must be satisfied; ultimate discretion rests with the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfaction of every substantive criterion in §29.7(b) is required; Administrator exercises discretion in judging whether those criteria are met, informed by discussion and stakeholder input described elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on 'splintering' — narrowly specialized, nontransferable occupations (§29.7(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator would not recognize as suitable an occupation if the scope of apprenticeship training is confined to a narrowly specialized subset of skills and competencies within an established occupation that are not readily transferable between employers in the sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is intended to prevent fragmentation of occupations into narrow, employer-specific skill sets. Sponsors should demonstrate that skills/competencies are broadly transferable across employers in the sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on replication of significant work processes without advancement (§29.7(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may decline a favorable suitability determination where the occupation under adjudication replicates a significant portion of the work processes from another occupation previously approved as suitable for registered apprenticeship without leading to a more advanced occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if an approved occupation includes 48 competencies and leads to professional certification, a new occupation that replicates some but not all of those competencies and would not lead to certification could be declined. The Administrator will consult industry leaders/stakeholders, analyze feedback holistically (not allowing a single stakeholder to veto), and consider whether replication across multiple prior occupations creates splintering. Replication that results in a more advanced/stackable occupation (e.g., Boilermaker I vs II) is treated differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, reasoning, and publication of unfavorable suitability determinations (§29.7(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Administrator determines an occupation is not suitable for registered apprenticeship, the Administrator would notify the applicant, provide the Administrator's reasoning, and publish the final agency determination on an OA public-facing website in compliance with FOIA proactive disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may reapply after addressing identified issues; Administrator may reevaluate and approve if criteria are met. Publication ensures transparency of determinations and rationales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit adjustments to existing suitable occupations (§29.7(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustments to existing suitable occupations, work processes, duration, or other significant adjustments in scope must be submitted to and approved by the Administrator to remain valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because occupations may change over time due to industry needs or technology, sponsors must submit revisions so Registration Agencies and OA can ensure standards remain relevant and continue to provide required training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year periodic review of suitability and standards (§29.7(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrator would review existing occupations determined suitable for registered apprenticeship on a 5-year cycle to determine continued suitability and consistency of work process schedules and related instruction outlines with industry standards; the same substantive criteria as §29.7(b) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator would seek public comment and stakeholder input per §29.7(d), notify programs in writing if revisions are required (programs must submit updated standards to their Registration Agency before the next training cycle), and if an occupation is no longer suitable programs cannot register apprentices in that occupation after the current cycle ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written standards of apprenticeship required (§29.8 general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every registered apprenticeship program must have a written set of standards of apprenticeship that include specified provisions (eligibility, selection, recruitment area, training approach, work process schedules, related instruction, trainer qualifications, credentials, wages for instruction time, assessment, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed §29.8 elaborates and strengthens minimum standards, adding topics such as cost transparency, protections against violence/intimidation/retaliation, and clearer structural requirements. Sponsors should include all required elements in their written standards submitted to Registration Agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum eligibility requirements and starting age (§29.8(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must establish the minimum eligibility requirements for program entry; minimum starting age not less than 16 years, though the minimum could be higher if required by Federal, State, or local law (e.g., 18 for electricians in some circumstances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must state eligibility criteria in standards and ensure compliance with applicable legal minimum ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection procedures must conform to EEO rules and Uniform Guidelines (§29.8(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Program selection procedures must conform to 29 CFR 30.10, comply with the Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (41 CFR part 60-3) including disparate impact evaluation and business necessity for adverse impacts, be applied uniformly, comply with the ADA and its implementing regs (29 CFR part 1630), and be facially neutral with respect to protected characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may use any method(s) for selection if compliant. Selection procedures must be submitted in the written plan for program standards and approved by the Registration Agency. Existing sponsors in compliance need not change practices; new programs must comply and may seek subregulatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to describe recruitment area in program standards (§29.8(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors must include a description of their recruitment area for new apprentices in the written program standards (e.g., range of miles from sponsor location, residents of a State or counties, online recruitment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes transparency and access, aids OA/SAAs/stakeholders in outreach (e.g., Apprenticeship Finder), supports EEO obligations for universal outreach/recruitment (29 CFR 30.3(b)), and helps identify local partners and resources. The requirement is not new substantively (already part of part 30) but relocates the information into the standards for clarity and outreach benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary on-the-job training approach with 2,000-hour minimum (§29.8(a)(4)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes eliminating separate time-based/competency-based/hybrid approaches and instituting a unitary approach requiring a uniform minimum term of on-the-job apprenticeship training of not fewer than 2,000 hours, combined with a requirement that the program provide all skills and competencies necessary to become proficient in the occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unitary approach links minimum durational requirement to competency attainment to prevent very-short programs and ensure apprentices reach proficiency. It resembles the current hybrid model but sets 2,000 hours as a minimum baseline to maintain program quality and international comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to 2,000-hour minimum for advanced standing or accelerated progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2,000-hour requirement may be greater per customary industry standards for some occupations; it may be reduced on a case-by-case basis for individual apprentices who are granted advanced standing/credit for prior learning or where an apprentice makes accelerated progress (§29.8(a)(20) referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors may request reductions when justified by prior learning/credit or documented accelerated competency attainment. Programs should document and justify advanced standing or credit in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum related instruction — 144 hours per 2,000 on-the-job hours (§29.8(a)(4)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered apprenticeship programs must provide a minimum average of 144 hours of related instruction in technical subjects relevant to the occupation for every 2,000 hours of on-the-job training; this is proposed as a requirement rather than a recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department invites comment on whether 144 hours is sufficient or should be higher (e.g., 20% off-the-job as used in some countries equates to 400 hours). Sponsors may count contact hours, credit hours, or convert credit to clock hours. Considerations include safety, EEO, anti-harassment training, and whether occupation-specific standards should set different minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of occupation(s), work process schedules, and related instruction outlines (§29.8(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include the program's occupation(s), work process schedules, and related instruction outlines; sponsors may submit standards for multiple occupations but must include these items for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing related instruction outlines gives Registration Agencies a clear understanding of the breadth and quality of off-the-job curriculum and its relevance to achieving proficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of related instruction provider and instructional methods (§29.8(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must identify the related instruction provider and the instructional methods used to deliver related instruction (e.g., in-person classroom, occupational/industry courses, web-based platforms, or other approved methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This creates a record of instructional modes, helping the Department understand prevalence and types of delivery; such information is also collected via ETA 671 Section I but is now required in standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation of trainer and instructor qualifications (§29.8(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must include an attestation that the qualifications and experience of trainers and instructors providing on-the-job training and related instruction satisfy the requirements in proposed §29.12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement serves as an explicit acknowledgment that trainer/instructor qualification standards will be met and must be submitted as part of the application in the standards under §29.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of interim credentials and postsecondary credit (§29.8(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must describe interim credentials received during the term, industry-portable occupational qualifications/licenses/certifications available upon completion, and any postsecondary credit an apprentice receives or may be eligible to receive from partnering educational institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department is collecting this information for transparency to apprentices about credentials and credits they will obtain; there is no requirement to provide additional credentials or credits, but programs that do must report them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement on whether related instruction time counts as hours worked and compensation (§29.8(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must state whether time spent in related instruction counts as hours worked, and if so, specify the wage rate and any fringe benefits for those hours; sponsors must comply with Federal, State, or local legal requirements (e.g., FLSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring this statement ensures apprentices are informed and that sponsors consider compensation for related instruction; sponsors may choose to pay even if not legally required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for regular assessment and feedback to apprentices (§29.8(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must set forth a process for regularly assessing and providing feedback to apprentices regarding acquisition of job-related knowledge, skills, and competencies during on-the-job training; feedback must be inclusive and accessible to all apprentices, including those with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expands on periodic review requirements by requiring documented assessment processes and feedback sharing. It complements duration and curriculum requirements by coupling time/work processes with structured assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable recruitment and retention plan as condition of registration (§29.10(a)(4) reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors, as a condition for program registration, must submit a written plan for equitable recruitment and retention of apprentices, which may describe partnerships to provide supportive services to apprentices facing impediments to completing the minimum training term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision is intended to ensure that apprentices who face structural barriers can sustain participation in longer-duration programs (e.g., 2,000-hour minimum), by identifying supports and partnerships (e.g., childcare, transportation, supportive services).

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs must undertake measures to ensure apprentices are free from violence, intimidation, and retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered apprenticeship programs must undertake effective measures to ensure apprentices are free from violence, intimidation, and retaliation in the workplace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit safeguard the proposed §29.8 seeks to add beyond existing minimum standards to protect apprentices' welfare; programs should include policies and procedures addressing these protections in their standards and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost transparency and reasonableness requirement for programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.8 would extend minimum standards to include establishing a cost transparency and reasonableness requirement for registered apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should disclose costs to apprentices and ensure costs are reasonable; the Department has proposed this to strengthen program quality and protect apprentices from undue financial burdens. Specific implementation details may be provided elsewhere or in subregulatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing program components to be addressed in standards (wages, ratios, safety, probation, advanced standing/credit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards must address key program components such as progressively increasing wages, apprentice-to-journeyworker ratios, work process schedules, safety requirements, probationary periods, and advanced standing and credit (components that the current regulation already addresses and which the proposed rule further elaborates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements remain foundational to the labor standards of apprenticeship; the proposed revisions reorganize and strengthen these requirements while adding new elements described above.
